item.title: GSEs boost foreclosure prevention as forbearances surge
item.description: Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac increased foreclosure prevention actions in October 2025, with forbearances and refinances rising as rates fell.

item.title: Chris Heller joins PLACE as chief revenue officer
item.description: Heller will oversee revenue strategy — including pricing, customer acquisition, retention and cross-platform integration.

item.title: Newfi Lending expands DSCR program to accept crypto reserves
item.description: Newfi’s updated DSCR loan guidelines let investors use up to 50% of crypto mutual funds or ETFs as reserves, expanding financing options.

item.title: Mortgage pros warn credit card rate cap could backfire on homebuyers
item.description: In the mortgage industry, the initial reaction to President Donald Trump’s proposal to cap credit card interest rates at 10% has been concern that the policy could ultimately backfire on would-be homebuyers.

item.title: NAR outlines legal risk mitigation, litigation strategy in 2025 report
item.description: NAR’s 2025 report highlights new legal counsel, department restructuring and policy changes to reduce litigation risk and exposure.

item.title: Digging into how an institutional investor ban would play out
item.description: Trump’s executive order attempts to block large institutional investors from buying single-family homes, but there is a carve out for BTR.

item.title: New deduction may lower seniors’ Social Security tax burden
item.description: For some retirees, the change could eliminate federal income taxes entirely, although many were already exempt from Social Security taxes.

item.title: AmeriTrust hires Shea Pallante as it preps for correspondent lending launch
item.description: AmeriTrust Mortgage Corp. has appointed Shea Pallante as chief revenue officer as the lender pursues a growth strategy that includes expanding into nondelegated correspondent channels and more than doubling its monthly origination volume.

item.title: Tapping a 401(k) for homeownership is risky business, experts say
item.description: Only about 40% of Americans are on track to meet retirement needs, and the average saver faces a $5,000 annual shortfall in retirement.
